request: Create a source-argument lesson in which students trace a narrowly scoped correction and revise a citation without dismissing unrelated claims.
objective: Apply a correction to its specified claim while retaining uncertainty about claims it does not address.

sources.text: Fictional local-history article: paragraph 2 says the library opened in 1912; paragraph 5 says the reading room had oak tables. The packet includes no original documents for either statement.
The publisher’s correction explicitly replaces “1912” in paragraph 2 with “1921”. It says the notice addresses the opening year only and makes no finding about the furniture.
A student writes: “Because the opening year was corrected, the article proves the tables were not oak.”
